algorithms.html: In particular, web applications may want to use performance information to:

steps.html: Control non-essential tasks and requests; e.g., allow or block 3rd party scripts, use or avoid heavy libraries.

Adjust the complexity of web content; e.g., the resolution and format for images and video, the compression level for uploading data, enable or disable computationally heavy operations such as animations, improve resource management (lazy loading, prefetching, prerendering).
Improve real user monitoring; e.g., better understand if users have faster or slower devices, focus development effort more appropriately.
Run computations on the client side vs. on the server side; e.g., use server-side rendering, run AI applications and LLMs on the client side.
Select ads that are better suited for the user device.

algorithms.name: compute the performance tier
algorithms.html: To compute the performance tier of a user device’s CPU:

steps.html: Let cores be the number of cores of the CPU as reported by the operating system, or null if the operating system does not report a core count.

algorithms.name: Navigator/cpuPerformance
algorithms.html: The cpuPerformance getter steps are:

steps.html: Let tier be the result of computing the performance tier of the device’s CPU, possibly with model-based adjustments as described in § 3.1 Computing Performance Tier Value.
